title: Choose the visual world for Slabbed
question: Layout stays catalogue → listing → cart → checkout. The roll assigned The Binder Page. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Binder Page
options.lineage: nine-pocket collector binder sheets and index tabs
options.thesis: Browsing is flipping through a collector's binder: every listing sits in its own clear pocket.
materials: clear vinyl pockets with a glint
options.viewport: Top bar as the binder spine with coloured index tabs; the catalogue grid as a pocket sheet on a navy cover; pagination as a page turn.
options.risk: Sheen and page turns turn gimmicky if they ever slow scanning of grades and prices.

raised.raise: Keyboard-first: / focuses search, ← and → turn binder pages.
State reads by form, not only colour: each payment state keeps its own glyph plus a progress rail on the order page.
Every press answers instantly: pockets and buttons swap state on press with no easing wait.
Price is the loudest type on every tile, one confident display grotesk.
One motion grammar: every move 0.4s with a small overshoot, nothing else.

options.label: The Card-Show Case
options.lineage: dealer glass cases at a coin and card show
options.thesis: Every listing laid on velvet in a lit dealer's case, with its price tag on a string.
materials: glass case edge with overhead spotlight
options.viewport: Catalogue rows read as lit glass cases; tiles sit on velvet with a hanging tag for price; hovering moves the spotlight onto that slab.
options.risk: Dark premium ground is where many runs land, and hanging tags can crowd the spec strip.

options.label: Drop Tag
options.lineage: industrial streetwear: quoted labels, zip-tie tags, hazard stripes
options.thesis: Listings announced like a streetwear drop: literal quoted labels, orange zip-tie price tags.
options.viewport: Filters as square caps label plates ("COINS" "CARDS"); tiles carry an orange zip-tie price tag; sold items take a hazard stripe.
options.case: Card and sneaker collecting share drop culture, so it lands with the audience; loses narrowly on trust, since hazard stripes near money can read as alarm.
options.risk: The quote-mark joke tires fast and stripes near payment states can look like errors.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The marketplace as a typed transcript on glass.
options.risk: Collectors don't browse slabs as text; photos lose.
options.case: Loses both axes: no collector identification, and photos of the item are the product.

options.label: Emission Line Rail
options.thesis: Everything hangs off one calibrated rail; state is line form.
options.viewport: Destinations as ticks on one rail.
options.risk: Abstract; hides the grid shoppers expect.
options.case: Loses both axes: foreign to collectors and obscures browsing.
options.kept: State carried by form, not hue alone.

options.label: Garden Guide Map
options.thesis: Flat colour lobes and capsule controls.
options.viewport: One swelling colour lobe per screen.
options.risk: Playful but says nothing about coins or cards.
options.case: Loses both axes: fun without collector identity, lobes fight a dense grid.
options.kept: One motion grammar with a small overshoot.

options.label: Elbow Panel Console
options.thesis: Pastel pill blocks on black, elbows as the grid.
options.risk: A fan costume on a payments product.
options.case: Loses both axes: borrowed fandom, confusing money states.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.thesis: Letters behave as matter and weather.
options.viewport: Words forming and breaking across the page.
options.case: Loses both axes: motion on money text harms clarity.
options.kept: One confident display grotesk carrying the loudest number.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: eBay / Mercari / Depop, executed at full craft: white ground, photo-first grid, one blue accent.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor expects, polished, with hover and add-to-cart feedback.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
